clue.text: One of the Rs in Berkshire

definitions.meaning: the three Rs of basic schooling are ..., writing and arithmetic
The county town of Berkshire, in southern England

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which letter R turns up in the name of an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rs' looks like letters in the word Berkshire, but it is the three Rs of education; Berkshire is an English county west of London, and Reading is its largest town.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling's basic trio is reading, writing and arithmetic, and the Berkshire town carries the same name.

clue.text: Debate 'About a Boy'

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived 'regarding', a standard crossword word for about
a boy is someone's son

explanation.surface: A discussion of Nick Hornby's novel and film 'About a Boy'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest the book title; the three words are simply worked through as pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone is to argue or discuss logically, which is what debating involves.

clue.text: Is its companion volume 'Mid to ZZZ' minute?

definitions.text: Is its companion volume 'Mid to ZZZ'
definitions.meaning: a two-volume dictionary splits the alphabet in two; this sense asks for the first volume, whose spine label, run together, is the answer
minute here means tiny, extremely small

explanation.surface: A bookish question about whether the second volume of a reference set is a tiny one.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as A TO MIC, the spine label of the first half of a two-volume reference work; its partner covers the rest of the alphabet, from Mid onwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic is used informally for something extremely small, as tiny as an atom; split up it is also a volume's alphabetical range.

clue.text: Repeats it: limited spells allowed online?

parts.note: E- is the prefix for electronic, online versions of things
rations are limited allowances or portions, the amounts one is allowed

explanation.surface: Someone renews a library item online, but only a limited number of times are permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spells' here means stints or portions, not magic; the online version of rations gets the e- prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterations are repetitions of a process, so the plural noun matches repeats used as a noun.

clue.text: Gaston's girl finds home for large tenor

indicators.note: the girl's name gives the letter a place to live, so it is put inside her name

parts.note: in the musical Gigi, Gaston falls for the title character Gigi
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's girlfriend finds lodging for a big singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Not quite a full house upstairs?

definitions.meaning: in poker a full house is three of a kind plus a pair; a lower hand that comes close
in old British usage '...' meant on the second floor, two flights of stairs up

explanation.surface: A theatre or home that is not quite packed, with the spare seats upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The poker sense is familiar; the second needs the dated British phrase 'two-pair back', a room on the second floor reached by two pairs of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker hand ranking below a full house, and an old term for a second-floor room, high in a building.

clue.text: … what's made by hasty judge putting these together side by side

definitions.text: … what's made by hasty judge putting these together side by side

parts.words: … what's made by hasty judge putting these together side by side
parts.note: 'these' are the two pairs of 5 across, and the clue's own number is 5

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a rash judge places these items next to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is number 5, and putting two and two together to make five is jumping to a wrong conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Two and two side by side give a sum that a hasty reasoner gets wrong, the idiom of rash inference.

clue.text: See 17
One taking on water, was square rig just out of trim?

indicators.note: trim here means the edges cut away, so each of these four words loses its first and last letter

explanation.surface: A sailing ship with a badly set square rig ships water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of trim' sounds nautical, but it strips the outer letters from each of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarius, the zodiac sign, is the water-carrier, pictured pouring or bearing water.

clue.text: What you might catch from wet pet animal

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, so the answer is a sound heard

parts.note: wet weather is rain, and pet is a term of endearment like dear

explanation.surface: Wondering what infection you could pick up from a soggy household pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' suggests an illness from a pet; it means hearing. Rain, dear, said aloud, gives the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer is an Arctic deer, a large hoofed animal.

clue.text: Agreed in the second year of life?

definitions.text: in the second year of life
definitions.meaning: a child aged one has completed a year and is in the second

explanation.surface: A toddler, past the first birthday, has agreed to something.
explanation.definitionFit: People at one share a view; a child at one has started its second year of life.

clue.text: Around La Méditerranée, say, negligently lug oil vessels

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the sea, holding it within them
done carelessly, so the letters of lug oil are carelessly jumbled

parts.note: La Méditerranée is a mer, French for sea; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Careless people lug containers of olive oil around the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negligently' scrambles LUG OIL into GLOULI, and 'Around' wraps it round MER, French for sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Glomeruli are tiny tufts of capillaries in the kidney, blood vessels that filter the blood.

clue.text: Changes in number of electrons spinning on axis do it

indicators.note: spinning sends the letters of on axis do it round into a new order

explanation.surface: Electrons spinning on an axis change in number, a physics-lesson picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning on axis' looks like science but 'spinning' scrambles ON AXIS DO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxidation, in chemistry, is the loss of electrons by an atom, a change in its electron count.

clue.text: George Russell, international driver, starts from here

definitions.text: George Russell, international driver, starts from here

indicators.note: the starts of these four words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The Formula One driver George Russell lines up at the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: George Russell is a British Formula One driver; the opening letters of his description spell where a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The grid is the marked starting area where racing cars line up before the race.

clue.text: Freedom for someone I trust to judge anagrams so indirect

definitions.text: Freedom for someone I trust to judge

indicators.note: the verb anagrams says the words so indirect are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter gives a trusted judge leeway to rule on indirect anagram clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagrams' looks like a noun after 'judge' but is the verb that rearranges SO INDIRECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion is the latitude to decide as one thinks fit, given to someone whose judgement is trusted.

clue.text: Put down in error, the writer attends brief jaunt, but gatecrashes

indicators.note: the group of pieces barges inside the writer's word like an uninvited guest

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
to be at an event is to attend it, so is at

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the trip is dropped

parts.note: a jaunt is a short trip
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer joins a short outing but turns up uninvited and gets the credit wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts TRIP to TRI; ISAT, TRI and BUT then gatecrash ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To misattribute is to credit something to the wrong source, recording it mistakenly.

clue.text: Like controlling obsession with Big Apple paraphernalia?

indicators.note: to control is to hold in, so the short word holds the rest

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
New York City's nickname is the Big Apple, abbreviated NY
to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

explanation.surface: A collector is controllingly obsessed with New York souvenirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just links NY and THING, the phrase 'a NY thing'; AS holds them both.
explanation.definitionFit: Anythings is a playful plural for all sorts of odds and ends, a catch-all for miscellaneous gear.

clue.text: See 17
Measures up, unlike naughty kid in Clarks?

definitions.text: Measures up, unlike naughty kid in Clarks?

parts.words: Measures up, unlike naughty kid in Clarks?
parts.note: Clarks is a British shoe shop where children's feet are measured

annotation.spelling: ACTS ONE'S AGE NOT ONE'S SHOE SIZE

explanation.surface: A well-behaved shopper, unlike the unruly child being fitted for shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clarks is a British high-street shoe retailer known for measuring children's feet; the clue twists the playground taunt 'act your age, not your shoe size'.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving maturely meets expectations, whereas a badly behaved child acts with the maturity of a small number.

clue.text: Pepys may have taken one to make stock manager

parts.note: to hackney a phrase is to make it stock or trite through overuse
a sports team's coach is its manager

explanation.surface: A recipe for stock, followed by the person who oversees things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks culinary but means commonplace, as in stock phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys, the 17th-century London diarist, would ride in horse-drawn cabs for hire, like this one.

clue.text: Wide-angle lens just a boon, regular shots taken when climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the chosen letters run backwards
regular shots means every other letter is taken, at a steady interval

explanation.surface: A photographer finds a wide-angle lens handy for regular pictures taken while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lens' and 'shots' suggest photography; the even letters ESUTBO are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An obtuse angle is wider than a right angle, between ninety and one hundred and eighty degrees.

clue.text: See 17
'Lunchtime!', as Yogi pinches a piece of cake

indicators.note: to pinch is to steal and hold, so the words hold the answer among their letters

explanation.surface: Yogi Bear cries that it's lunchtime as he steals a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Yogi Bear, the cartoon bear, is famous for snatching picnic baskets, which makes 'pinches' natural in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for something simple to do.

clue.text: Be still say cheese off I click non-stop

parts.note: sh is the interjection telling someone to be quiet
to utter is to say
to cheese someone off is to annoy them, to bug them

explanation.surface: A photographer tells the subject to hold still and say cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say cheese' is a false phrase: 'say' and 'cheese off' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutterbug is an enthusiastic amateur photographer, constantly clicking the camera.

clue.text: Habitual drinker who's first to break this at party — but not last?

indicators.note: not last says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.words: first to break this at party
parts.note: someone breaks the ice at a party by starting conversation first

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker is first to get a party going, but not the last to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'break the ice'; dropping its last letter E leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Theic is a rare word for someone who drinks excessive amounts of tea, a habitual tea drinker.

clue.text: Spots origin of 18, so its driver told us?

indicators.note: a cab driver telling us the word aloud gives how it sounds in his accent

parts.note: the hackney carriage takes its name from Hackney, the East London district, which a Cockney says as 'Ackney, dropping the H

explanation.surface: A hint about where 18's name comes from, as relayed by its cab driver.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a district of East London; a London cabbie drops the H, and 'Ackney sounds like the skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition that brings out spots and pimples.

clue.text: Pure quality pub engineer as a one-off keeps

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the engineer is held within

parts.note: once means on a single occasion, as a one-off
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A pub and an engineer, one-off, keep something unspoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence is the quality of being blameless or untainted, which is purity.

clue.text: With reverse sweep Moeen Ali at last grabs single to secure Ashes?

indicators.note: a reverse sweep is a backhanded cricket stroke, so the assembled letters are reversed
grabs means takes hold of, so the last letters hold the run
at last means each of the two names gives its final letter

parts.note: a single in cricket is one run

explanation.surface: England cricketer Moeen Ali plays a reverse sweep for a single to win the Ashes series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England–Australia cricket series; 'Ashes?' here means a dead person's ashes, put into an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place cremated remains in an urn, keeping them safe.

clue.text: Festivals suspended at centre, when short becomes shorter

indicators.note: at centre picks out the single middle letter of suspended

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: becoming shorter means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: terse means short, curt

explanation.surface: Festivals are paused midway, when a short one is cut shorter still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes shorter' trims TERSE to TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Easters are the yearly Christian feasts celebrating the Resurrection, festivals in the church calendar.

clue.text: Sanction postal scam?

parts.note: a con is a scam, a swindle
postal suggests something sent through the post

explanation.surface: Authorities approve a fraud carried out by mail.
explanation.walkthrough: A con sent through the post is a postal scam.
explanation.definitionFit: Consent is permission or approval, which is what a sanction is.
